source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"NSAIDs increase renal lithium elimination, so concurrent use usually lowers the serum lithium concentration below the therapeutic range.","B":"NSAIDs can often decrease renal lithium clearance, raising serum lithium concentrations and increasing the risk of lithium toxicity.","C":"NSAIDs neutralize lithium in the gastrointestinal tract, so the main concern is loss of mood stabilization rather than toxicity.","D":"NSAIDs do not meaningfully interact with lithium, so no additional clinical or serum-level monitoring is needed when they are combined."}}
source_row.rationale: NSAIDs can reduce renal blood flow and lithium clearance, potentially leading to elevated lithium levels and increased risk of lithium toxicity when used concurrently. Clients taking lithium should generally avoid regular NSAID use when possible, or be monitored closely (including lithium level checks) if the combination is necessary.
source_row.source_detail: DailyMed lithium labeling, Drug Interactions 7.1: NSAIDs decrease renal blood flow/lithium clearance and can increase serum lithium; monitor concentrations. Label revised 2026-02; reviewed 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
